findings.evidence: `lang="translanguage"`
findings.fix: Set `lang` to the actual content language, e.g. `lang="en"`.
findings.violation: "translanguage" is not a valid BCP 47 language code, so screen readers and browsers cannot determine the page's language for pronunciation/translation purposes.

findings.evidence: `<title id="head-title"></title>`
findings.fix: Add a descriptive title, e.g. `<title>Rider service updates</title>`.
findings.violation: The page title is empty, so the browser tab, bookmarks, and screen reader announcements have no identifying text for this page.

findings.evidence: Both end with "Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Write a sentence specific to each action, or remove it from s1-p2 if staff don't actually assist with checking arrivals.
findings.location: Section s1, paragraphs s1-p1 and s1-p2
findings.violation: The same boilerplate closing sentence is reused for two different actions (requesting a fare adjustment vs. checking real-time arrivals); checking arrivals isn't really a "request" station staff process, making the second instance confusing/nonsensical.

findings.evidence: ``
findings.fix: Add a descriptive `alt` attribute (or `alt=""` if the image is purely decorative).
findings.violation: The image has no `alt` attribute at all, so assistive technology has no fallback text and will likely announce the filename instead.

findings.fix: Change this heading to `<h2>` (or `<h3>` if it's meant to nest under s1).
findings.violation: The heading level jumps from h2 directly to h4, skipping h3, which breaks the document outline for screen reader users navigating by heading level.

findings.evidence: Heading says "Accessibility improvements" but the paragraph is about reporting a service issue by phone and the table lists zone on-time status.
findings.fix: Rename the heading to match the actual content (e.g., "Service status") or replace the content with genuine accessibility-improvement information.
findings.location: Section s2, heading "Accessibility improvements" vs. its content (s2-p1, s2-table1)
findings.violation: The section heading does not match its content - nothing about accessibility (e.g., elevators, ramps, accommodations) is discussed.

findings.evidence: `<table id="s2-table1"><tr><th scope="col">Zone</th>...`
findings.fix: Add a `<caption>` such as "Zone status" inside the table.
findings.violation: The table has no `<caption>`, so screen reader users jumping to the table get no context about what it represents.

findings.evidence: Both contain the identical sentence "Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Write a sentence specific to each paragraph's actual topic.
findings.violation: The same sentence is duplicated verbatim across two unrelated topics (reporting a service issue vs. reviewing the schedule online), which is confusing boilerplate reuse rather than content tailored to each context.

findings.evidence: s2-p1: "Passengers can report a service issue by calling rider services." / s3-p1: "Passengers can report a service issue at any station kiosk."
findings.fix: Consolidate into one consistent statement listing all valid channels, or clarify how the two differ.
findings.violation: Two different sections state two different, uncoordinated channels for the same action ("report a service issue") without clarifying whether both are valid or which is preferred.

findings.evidence: "Route adjustments take effect on the posted effective date."
findings.fix: Provide the actual date or a link to where riders can find it.
findings.violation: The sentence references a "posted effective date" with no link, date, or pointer to where that date is actually posted, making it unactionable.

findings.evidence: `role="status"` wraps "Local residents can check real time arrivals through the online portal. A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Remove `role="status"` from this static content, or reserve it for an element whose content actually updates dynamically.
findings.violation: `role="status"` is meant for a live region that announces dynamic updates; applying it to static instructional text is a misuse of the ARIA role and will cause unnecessary/incorrect announcements.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can check real time arrivals through the online portal."
findings.fix: Use a consistent audience term throughout (e.g., "Riders").
findings.violation: "Local residents" is inconsistent with the terminology used elsewhere in the document ("Riders," "Passengers," "Commuters"), creating confusion about the intended audience.

findings.evidence: Both contain "A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Remove or rewrite the sentence in s3-statuscard to accurately describe checking arrivals.
findings.violation: This sentence is duplicated between reporting a service issue and checking real-time arrivals; the latter is not a "request" that gets "processed," so the reused sentence doesn't make sense there.

findings.evidence:
`
`
findings.fix: Use a native `<button>` element, and either remove this control or give it clear contextual purpose tied to actual content.
findings.location: Section s3, `<div class="icon-delete" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Delete item" id="s3-customcontrol">`
findings.violation: A custom non-native "Delete item" control appears with no stated purpose or connection to any list item or data in this rider-updates page, and it reimplements button semantics with a `<div>` instead of using a native `<button>`.

findings.evidence: Steps listed: "Choose a plan," "Enter payment details," "Confirm your order."
findings.fix: Remove this component or move it to the appropriate purchase flow page.
findings.violation: This payment/checkout wizard is unrelated to the page's subject (rider service updates: fares, accessibility, stations) and appears to be stray/misplaced content.

findings.evidence:
`
Choose a plan
` (and siblings)
findings.fix: Mark the steps up as an ordered list and indicate the current step with `aria-current="step"`.
findings.violation: The steps are plain unordered `<div>`s with no semantic list markup and no indication of which step is current (no `aria-current`), so assistive technology users get no sense of progress or structure.

findings.evidence: `click here`
findings.fix: Change the link text to something descriptive, e.g. "View the full list of upcoming fare adjustments."
findings.violation: "click here" is a non-descriptive link text that provides no context out of surrounding text, which is a known accessibility and usability issue for screen reader users who navigate by link list.

findings.evidence: `<form id="s3-form">` has no `action` or `method` attribute; none of its inputs (`select#topic`, `#email`, `#phone`, `#promo`) have a `name` attribute.
findings.fix: Add `name` attributes to each form control and an `action`/`method` to the `<form>` (or document that submission is handled entirely via JavaScript).
findings.violation: Without `name` attributes on the fields (and an `action`/`method` on the form), a standard form submission would send no usable data to any server endpoint.

findings.evidence: Label text "Phone number (required)" but `<input id="phone" type="tel" autocomplete="tel">`
findings.fix: Add `required` (and/or `aria-required="true"`) to the phone input to match its label.
findings.violation: The label tells users the field is required, but the input itself lacks the `required` attribute (and no `aria-required`), so there's no actual enforced or announced validation requirement.

findings.evidence: `<input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true">`
findings.fix: Only set `aria-invalid="true"` dynamically after validation fails, defaulting to `false` or omitted on load.
findings.violation: `aria-invalid="true"` is hardcoded in the markup regardless of actual input state, so screen readers will announce the field as invalid even before the user has entered anything.

findings.evidence: `<input id="promo" ... aria-invalid="true">` and `<span class="error-text" aria-live="polite" id="s3-form-promo-error">`
findings.fix: Add `aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error"` to the promo input.
findings.location: Section s3 form, promo field and its error text
findings.violation: The error message is not programmatically associated with the promo input (no `aria-describedby`), so screen reader users focused on the field won't hear why it's invalid.

findings.evidence: `<button type="submit" class="btn-primary" id="s3-form-submit" aria-label="Send form now">Submit</button>`
findings.fix: Remove the `aria-label` (letting the visible "Submit" text serve as the accessible name) or make the `aria-label` include "Submit."
findings.violation: The accessible name ("Send form now") does not contain the visible label text ("Submit"), which violates WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name) and confuses speech-input/screen-reader users trying to match what they see to what they hear.
